Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV. We can support a short-lived capacity uplift; here are the options we can implement quickly while protecting both sides from invoice surprises:

Option 1 — 48-72h temporary uplift (approved surge exception)
- Apply a temporary quota/rate ceiling increase for the requested window.
- Tokens above baseline billed at standard per-token rate + an 8% surge surcharge.
- Invoice as usual; surge surcharge will be a line item and we can cap total surge fees at $20k for the window.

Option 2 — Uplift with deferred true-up (no immediate surcharge)
- Allow the uplift but suspend automatic overrun invoice for 7 days.
- After the window, we reconcile: if FastRetail signs a 3-month pilot commitment within 30 days, we apply a 50% credit on the surge overage; otherwise standard billing applies.

Operational notes:
- We need an IP/egress allowlist (send to security@redwood.com) and a formal MOU to authorize the change.
- I attached a draft surge-exception MOU that documents window, cap, and reconciliation paths.

I’m looping in Marissa (Sales Ops) and Ben (Billing) to confirm approval and finalize pricing. If you confirm which option you prefer, we’ll execute the MOU and push the quota change.

—Chloe
